newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Long Distance says chairman resigned.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Long Distance says chairman resigned.

text.p: U.S. Long Distance Corp on Monday said its chief executive, Larry James, would take over as chairman after the resignation of Parris "Butch" Holmes Jr.

In connection with Holmes' resignation, the U.S. Long Distance board agreed to pay him a $875,000 cash bonus and grant him 25,000 shares of restricted common stock. The package will result in a one-time charge to third-quarter earnings, U.S. Long Distance said in a statement.
U.S. Long Distance shares dipped 3/16 to 15-5/16 Monday.

Holmes resigned as part of the company's spin-off of its Billing Information Concepts Corp subsidiary. He will continue his duties as chairman and chief executive of Billing Information, U.S. Long Distance said.
Holmes, who founded U.S. Long Distance in 1985, has acted as both the chairman of its board and the chairman and chief executive of Billing Information since the August 1996 spinoff.

James, who previously served as president and chief operating officer at U.S. Long Distance, was appointed chief executive in August 1996. The company provides communications service to business customers throughout the United States.
